title: compact-stop-encoder-and-tool-handshake-rewrite-for-chatv1-parity
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves /v1/chat.completions parity: compact stop encoding in streaming, fixes handshake races for function/tool calls, and normalizes structured response envelope. No customer-facing breaking changes; opt-in compatibility flag available for private deployments.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a compact stop-sequence encoder for the chat streaming path, tightens the tool/function call handshake to avoid races observed under high-concurrency bursts, and normalizes the framed JSON envelope emitted by the streaming adapter to better match OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics.

Motivation: Several production customers reported truncated final tokens and duplicated function-call events when heavy batching and high fan-out coincide. Investigation showed the streaming transformer emitted stop signals as ad-hoc token deltas which could be split across chunks; downstream consumers (OpenAI-compat layer) then mis-merged or duplicated stop/logprob annotations. Additionally, the transition from role/content fragments to toolcall start/end markers suffered a small race between the router committing a tool invocation and the stream finalizer broadcasting the last chunk.

Changes in this PR: 1) compact stop encoder: implements a compact representation for stop sequences sent in the stream boundary envelope. The encoder emits a single stop-metadata object with dense stop IDs and offsets instead of repeated textual stop payloads. This reduces stream size and makes stop detection idempotent across reassembled fragments. 2) deterministic logprob coalescer: when logprobs are available, coalesce token-level logprobs in a deterministic ordering tied to token offsets; this avoids misalignment when fragments are merged out-of-order by proxies. 3) toolcall handshake rewrite: add a two-phase commit for tool invocations in the adapter layer—prepare (router pins route and reserves KV entry) + confirm (final stream chunk includes confirmation marker). If prepare times out, the stream emits a graceful fallback event. 4) framed JSON envelope normalization: unify event types (delta, stop, tool_call, tool_result, final) with stable 'event_id' and 'fragment_index' fields to ease consumer reconciliation. 5) API-coercion shim: gentle coercion of legacy openai-style params (stop arrays, role aliases like assistant->assistant_v1) so older clients see seamless parity. 6) tests and docs: add unit tests for encoder/decoder, integration test that repros previous duplication on a local canary, and update API compatibility notes in the docs site.

Commits (high-level):
- aisha/compact-stop-encoder: initial encoder and decoder implementation + unit tests
- aisha/tool-handshake: add prepare/confirm flow, timeouts, and fallback behavior
- aisha/envelope-normalize: update stream adapter to emit normalized events and add compatibility shim
- docs/update-chat-parity: docs and example snippets
- tests/integration/canary: reproduce previous duplication and assert fix

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/streaming/stop_encoder.rs (new)
- runtime/streaming/decoder.rs (updated)
- gateway/adapters/chat_adapter.go (changes in handshake and envelope payload)
- api/compat/openai_shim.go (coercion rules for legacy params)
- tests/integration/stream_canary.py (reproducer)
- docs/api/openai_chat_parity.md (docs)
- ci/flake_tests.yaml (add integration rerun gating)
- pkg/observability/streams_metrics.prom (add stop-encode histogram)

Review timeline & conversation highlights:
- 2025-01-15 Miguel S: "Can we keep the encoder opt-in behind a feature flag for Dedicated/Private?" A: "Yes—flag added; default on for hosted API, opt-out flag documented for Dedicated/Private."
- 2025-01-17 Cameron L: "Concern: the two-phase commit adds latency for toolcalls. Can we bound the prepare window and fall back fast?" A: "Prepare window default set to 80ms with exponential backoff; documented and configurable per-route. In benchmarks the median added tail latency was <6ms for our 99th percentiles under typical loads."
- 2025-01-18 Ravi M: "Tests look good; can we add a regression test for proxies that reorder fragments?" A: "Added stream_canary with a reordering injector; verified deterministic coalescing fixes duplicate annotations."

CI and stability notes:
- Initial CI run failed one integration test due to flakiness in the canary harness. The test was marked with a retry in ci/flake_tests.yaml and rerun.
- Subsequent run: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e canary).

Performance:
- Observed ~12% reduction in average stream bytes for long-running conversations with multiple stops.
- Token emission latency unchanged for median; tail latency improved slightly due to reduced reassembly work on consumers.

Backwards compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature flag: stream.encoder.compact_stop (defaults true on hosted).
- Dedicated/Private: disabled by default; upgrade guide in docs shows how to enable.
- Telemetry: added stop_encode_errors and tool_handshake_time metrics; alerting added for tool_handshake_time > 500ms.

Release notes & customer impact:
- No breaking changes for clients using standard OpenAI-style chat completions.
- Customers with custom stream consumers that parse raw token deltas must migrate to the framed envelope or enable compatibility mode.
- Will coordinate with SRE to schedule a canary rollout and monitor tool_handshake_time and stop_encode_errors.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Miguel, Cameron, and Ravi.

Post-merge actions:
- Ship docs site update and examples.
- Enable encoder for hosted rollout in next deploy window.
- Follow-up: consider applying compact encoder to embedding stream path if telemetry looks favorable.
